Marcus ran hotter than forecast from 9:00 on shop equipment repair. His body temperature climbed about 0.075 °C more per half hour than predicted, over two slots. The job escalated from moderate to heavy to very heavy work in a short stretch. The plan treated it as a steadier load than it turned out to be, so the forecast underestimated how fast he would heat up. No alerts fired, so the gap stayed small. Still, the schedule was built on a too-optimistic picture of that task, and output came in at only about 71% of target.
insights: Treat shop equipment repair as a job that can ramp up to very heavy work. Plan it at the heaviest level it may reach, not the level it starts at.
When a task moves through several effort levels, split it into shorter blocks. Do the very heavy parts earlier in the morning, before 9:00 if possible, when heat load is lower.
After a heavy or very heavy block, follow it with a lighter task for the same worker instead of more heavy repair work.
Watch Marcus's actual heat rise on repair work for the next few days. If he keeps running hotter than forecast, plan his repair shifts as heavier from the start.

reflection.root_cause: Kofi is a new hire whose body is not yet used to the heat. From 11:00 he was moved from moderate work up to heavy and then very heavy shop equipment repair. Each half hour his body temperature rose about 0.25 °C more than the plan expected, because the forecast treated him like a worker who is already used to the heat. By 14:00 he reached 38.0 °C, above the high-end forecast of 37.7 °C, and spent 40 minutes in alert. The real problem was stacking harder and harder tasks on an unacclimatized worker during the hottest part of the day, all in the same job.
insights: Don't step a new hire up in effort (moderate to heavy to very heavy) across late morning and early afternoon. Keep Kofi at light or moderate work during the hottest hours.
Give the very heavy parts of shop equipment repair to an acclimatized worker. Pair Kofi on the lighter parts of that job so he still learns it.
If a new hire must do heavy work, schedule it early in the morning, before 11:00, and swap him onto a lighter task after that.
Plan new hires' heat build-up as faster than the standard forecast. Kofi's ran about 0.25 °C per half hour above forecast, so check on him earlier in heavy stretches instead of waiting for an alert.
